findings.clauses: ES-7, ES-9, RV-1 (session base), RV-5, FZ-3, EN-2, A4, Appendix B Baseline and Backstop; user mid-turn message 3
findings.problem:
Mid-turn message 3 arrived 2 minutes after v4 was saved. It requires two things during a session: the Current tab must be completely uneditable, and the base the session diffs from must be concrete and unchanging. v4 builds the opposite.
- ES-7 copies hand edits into the session's base and working copy as they happen.
- ES-9 still allows moving cards on Current, and keeps other subjects editable, including subjects whose declarations the session's subject imports.
- These all assume a moving base: RV-1's base ('plus your own changes'), RV-5 ('by a hand edit'), FZ-3 ('frozen value becomes your version'), EN-2 ('your own edits during the session'), A4, and Appendix B's Baseline ('plus what you typed … from your transforms') and Backstop ('session base plus your own edits').
A builder following v4 would implement exactly what the user has just ruled out.
findings.fix:
1. Replace ES-7 with: "ES-7 (v4) The base is fixed. A session diffs against your files exactly as they were when it started. While it is active, the session subject's Current view is completely read-only: no edits, arrows, moves, Tidy layout, A|P box or Undo. Subjects whose declarations it uses are read-only too. If those files change on disk anyway (a hand edit in VS Code), telelean does not merge the change. The session bar says 'your files changed since this session started', and Apply is refused until you revert the change or Exit. Freezing stays available, because it changes neither your files nor the base." Tag it '(yours: turn-21 message 3)'.
2. RV-1: the base is 'your files at the session's start'.
3. Delete 'or by a hand edit, ES-7' (RV-5), the ES-7 sentence in FZ-3, 'your own edits during the session' (EN-2), and 'plus your own edits' (Backstop).
4. Rewrite A4 to describe the refusal.
5. Appendix B Baseline: your in-session transform edits become accepted items in the working copy instead of joining the base.
6. ES-9: drop 'Moving cards still works' and narrow 'Other subjects stay editable'.

findings.clauses: RV-6, BD-6, RV-5, §13 item 6, A15, ★D8 slice 1
findings.problem:
v4 makes the green glow transitive: established means proved all the way down to axiom cards. Proving a pending target therefore turns every card that rests on it from blue with 'rests on pending' to green in the Proposed view.
RV-6 hides only things 'into that target', so these downstream glows and chips show whether the proof succeeded before the user has judged its statements.
The same leak happens through another target's Result. A's Result can be revealed while L's is still hidden, and A's verdict ('established' vs 'rests on pending L') tells you L's outcome. RV-6's reveal condition waits only for statement and belief items.
This breaks D-19 and the §13.6 guarantee in v4's main new workflow (A15: draw an arrow into a used axiom, then formalize it).

findings.clauses: AR-5, ES-2 (preset, third exception), RV-1 (Add premise, Add arrow), B.3, FZ-13
findings.problem:
A target can be selected through its 'follows from nothing' mark. Its Dependencies are then open for additions, so Claude may propose Add premise or Add arrow items into it (RV-1 checks 'the target's question plus it'). Accepting one leaves a card with both the mark (the explicitly empty set) and an incoming arrow.
AR-5 removes the mark only when you draw an arrow, and B.3 forbids Claude to touch it. The spec never says what happens. Freezing a mark is also meaningless as written: 'Claude may not remove them' adds nothing, because Claude can never remove a mark.
